**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Remove rST markup from the test docstring**

Because this is a test docstring and is not rendered by Sphinx, the repository convention explicitly forbids double-backtick inline literals; write tool_calls[].index and index=None as plain prose rather than adding rST markup here.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L44-L51](https://github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-py/blob/03710ca8560f2e6702151f625312f0ec4aaf98b1/AGENTS.md#L44-L51)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep repeated-name fragments in one unindexed call**

For an OpenAI-compatible backend that omits both the index and ID but repeats `function.name` on each streamed fragment, this condition is true for every fragment, so arguments such as `{"city":` and `"Paris"}` are emitted as two invalid tool calls instead of being accumulated into one. The previous None-index lookup kept these fragments together, so the new boundary heuristic should not treat every repeated name as a new call.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->
Done in 60a56d110: the test docstring is plain prose now (no rST double backticks).

Good catch, fixed in 60a56d110. A fragment without an id no longer starts a call, even when it repeats the function name, so `{"city":` and `"Paris"}` stay together as before. Only a new id starts a new call. The new test for that case fails on the previous commit and passes now.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Match unindexed fragments against all stored IDs**

When an OpenAI-compatible backend interleaves fragments for parallel unindexed calls while repeating each call ID (for example, `A, B, A, B`), this compares an ID only with the most recently stored call. Both revisits are therefore treated as new calls, yielding four partial tool calls instead of two complete ones in the OpenAI, LiteLLM, and AI Guard reducers; search the existing unindexed entries for tool_id before appending, and only fall back to the latest call when no ID is available.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Right, fixed in 3994d7c92. Interleaved fragments (`A, B, A, B`) that repeat each id were compared only with the latest call. An id is now looked up among all stored calls and only starts a new call when none carries it; a fragment without an id still continues the latest call. The new test with the interleaved case fails on the previous commit and passes now.
